   City Council Staff Report
DATE:  MAY 11, 2026

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

FROM:  CITY ATTORNEY’S OFFICE

DISTRICT:  ALL

SUBJECT:  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. CC 2026-029, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE EXPRESSING THE
  CITY COUNCIL’S OPPOSITION TO MEASURE ER, A LOS ANGELES
  COUNTYWIDE INITIATIVE, ON THE JUNE 2026 STATEWIDE
  BALLOT

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommend that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2026-029, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
  Palmdale expressing the City Council’s opposition to Measure ER, a Los Angeles
  Countywide initiative on the June 2026 statewide ballot; and,

  2. Direct staff to continue legal analysis and intergovernmental coordination related
  to Countywide tax policy and local fiscal autonomy.

BACKGROUND:

This item is presented at the request of the City Council on May 5, 2026, for consideration
to express a formal position regarding Measure ER, a Los Angeles County ballot measure
appearing on the June 2026 statewide ballot.

DISCUSSION

Measure ER may create fiscal, operational, or administrative impacts affecting the City
and its residents. The measure proposes a Countywide 0.5% transaction and use tax
increase that would apply uniformly across Los Angeles County, including in Palmdale.

Measure ER revenues are not legally required to be allocated in proportion to the amounts
collected within Palmdale. Allocation decisions would remain subject to the County’s
budgetary discretion.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Reso. No. CC 2026-029
May 11, 2026
Page 2

The attached resolution is presented for the City Council’s consideration to formally state
its position on Measure ER. The City Council may also consider directing staff to evaluate
or pursue additional actions related to local fiscal autonomy and Countywide tax policy,
including:

    Coordinating with similarly situated gateway and suburban cities
    Engaging with the League of California Cities regarding regional tax policy impacts
    Continuing legal analysis regarding potential conflicts with the statewide sales tax
  cap
    Conducting legislative or intergovernmental advocacy with Los Angeles County
  and the State
    Providing public information regarding cumulative tax burdens on residents and
  businesses
    Assessing potential post-election legal options, if warranted

Adoption of the attached resolution would formally state the City Council’s position on
Measure ER and direct staff to continue coordinated legal and intergovernmental analysis
related to Countywide tax policy and local fiscal autonomy.

FISCAL IMPACT

$0; There is no fiscal impact associated with this action. Adoption of the attached
Resolution does not authorize any expenditure of public funds.

   CITY COUNCIL
  CITY OF PALMDALE, CALIFORNIA
  RESOLUTION NO. CC 2026-029

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE
  EXPRESSING THE CITY’S OPPOSITION TO MEASURE ER, A LOS
  ANGELES COUNTYWIDE INITIATIVE, ON THE JUNE 2026 STATEWIDE
  BALLOT.

  WHEREAS, Measure ER is a Los Angeles County (“County”) ballot
measure scheduled to appear on the June 2026 election ballot;

  WHEREAS, the City Council has reviewed the text of Measure ER and
evaluated its potential fiscal, operational, and service‑level impacts on the
residents and businesses of the City of Palmdale (“City”);

  WHEREAS, Measure ER proposes a Countywide transaction and use tax
increase of 0.5%, which would apply to City residents, regardless of local income
levels, cost of living, or regional service levels provided in the Antelope Valley;

  WHEREAS, City residents already pay one of the highest combined sales
tax rates in Los Angeles County and California;

  WHEREAS, the City Council is concerned that additional Countywide
transaction and use taxes reduce the remaining local revenue capacity available
for cities to address future local infrastructure, public safety, transportation, parks,
and quality of life needs through locally controlled funding measures;

  WHEREAS, Measure ER revenues are not legally restricted to
geographically proportional service delivery within the City of Palmdale, and future
allocations remain subject to County budgetary discretion;

  WHEREAS, the Antelope Valley’s geographic distance from the County’s
urban core creates unique service-delivery and transportation challenges that
warrant careful consideration when imposing additional Countywide taxes on local
residents;

  WHEREAS, City households have a median income significantly lower than
many other regions of the County, and an increase in sales tax could have a
disproportionate impact on City’s residents, who already face higher transportation
costs and greater travel distances for many County-administered services;

  WHEREAS, the City Council desires to protect local fiscal autonomy and
prevent overreliance on regressive taxation; and
 Resolution No. CC 2026-029
Page 2 of 3

  WHEREAS, the City Council is considering this matter in a public meeting
to ensure transparency, to allow residents to hear the City’s analysis of how
Measure ER may affect local tax burdens and County service allocations, and to
provide an open forum for public understanding of the measure’s potential impacts.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the City Council of the City of Palmdale
as follows:

  SECTION 1. The City Council hereby specifically finds that all of the facts
  set forth in the Recitals are true and correct and constitute the findings of the
  City Council in this matter.

  SECTION 2. The City Council, after reviewing the potential impacts of
  Measure ER on Palmdale residents and City operations, hereby expresses its
  opposition to Measure ER based on the informational findings identified in this
  Resolution.

  SECTION 3. This resolution shall take effect immediately upon its
  adoption.

  SECTION 4. The City Clerk shall certify the adoption of this resolution.

  PASSED, APPROVED, and ADOPTED this 11th day of May, 2026.
